summary: sudoku-term postinstall auto-executes an opaque ~34 MB Go binary shipped in place of the documented 26 KB C helper
details: The package's scripts/postinstall.js resolves prebuilt/linux-x64/sudoku-hint through src/hint.js nativeBinaryPath() and runs it with --selftest via execFileSync on every npm install. README documents this artifact as a 26 KB statically-musl-linked ELF built from the shipped ~200-line native/hint.c (stdio.h/string.h only) and states the binary 'reads no files, opens no sockets'. The actually shipped Linux binary is 33,976,468 bytes and is a Go executable containing runtime metadata (runtime., GODEBUG, chacha8) and imports for net/http, crypto/tls, and os/exec — full network, TLS, and subprocess-execution capability that the advertised C source cannot produce and that the README explicitly denies. There is no hash or signature verification on the binary before execution. The postinstall lifecycle hook therefore auto-executes attacker-supplied native code with undisclosed network/exec capability on any machine that runs npm install for this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
